cases.label: midnight minus 2 ms on datetime: the result is the .997 tick, kept at 3 digits (not .998, not rounded to the second)
cases.reasoning: T-SQL DATEADD(millisecond, -2, datetime '2004-07-01') lands on the datetime tick .997 (3.33 ms resolution). PostgreSQL interval arithmetic would give .998; the conversion hard-codes .997 and returns timestamp(3). A timestamp(0) or a date return type, or the exact -2 ms, would differ from the value SQL Server returns. This function has no parameter and reads no table, so the empty call is the only input that exists; the case necessarily repeats the hand-derived case. It is kept because the adversarial gate and its planted-defect check run on the adversarial cases alone, without the hand-derived ones. The planted defect 'end date is exactly 2 ms before midnight' is caught only through this call.
